definition_zh: n. 冷漠；无兴趣；缺乏热情（尤指对公共事务）
definition_en: A lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern, especially about matters that most people think important; the state of not caring either way.
core_image: 心里那根弦松了，对什么都提不起劲
scene: 选民对这场辩论毫无反应，投票率低得惊人。Voter apathy kept turnout below forty per cent.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：apathy 指对本该关心的事提不起兴趣，voter apathy 就是选民懒得投票的那种集体冷淡。

senses.title: No interest or enthusiasm
senses.definition: a state in which someone feels no interest in or excitement about something that would normally matter
senses.definitionCN: 对本该在意的事情既不感兴趣也不激动的状态
senses.example: Apathy among students made the new club hard to launch.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们的冷淡让这个新社团很难办起来。
senses.why: The prefix a- means without and pathos means feeling, so the word literally names a state with the feeling removed.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a- 意为「无」，pathos 意为「感受」，所以这个词字面上就是「把感受抽掉之后的状态」。

senses.title: No concern for public matters
senses.definition: the collective indifference of a group towards politics, charity or shared problems, the sense used in voter apathy
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体对政治、公益或共同问题集体性的不关心，即 voter apathy 中的用法
senses.example: The report blamed public apathy for the slow response to the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把洪灾应对迟缓归因于公众的冷漠。
senses.why: Here the feeling is not missing from one person but from a crowd, so apathy becomes a social problem rather than a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 这里缺的不是一个人的感受，而是一整群人的感受，于是 apathy 从个人情绪变成了社会问题。

intro.en: Apathy comes from Greek apatheia, freedom from suffering, built from a-, without, and pathos, feeling. The Stoics admired it; English later turned it into a fault.
intro.cn: apathy 来自希腊语 apatheia「不受苦、无感」，由 a-「无」加 pathos「感受」构成。斯多葛学派把它当作修养，英语后来却把它变成了缺点。

items.en: Greek pathos meant suffering, and then feeling in general. It gives English pathos, sympathy, empathy and pathetic.
items.cn: 希腊语 pathos 意为「受苦」，进而泛指「感受」。它产生英语的 pathos、sympathy、empathy 与 pathetic。

items.en: Adding a-, without, gave apatheia, the Stoic goal of a mind unmoved by passion. It was praise, not blame.
items.cn: 加上 a-「无」得到 apatheia，即斯多葛派追求的「不为激情所动」的心境。这在当时是褒奖，不是指责。

items.en: Latin borrowed the term as apathia and kept it as a philosophical word for calm detachment.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 apathia，仍作为哲学术语，表示平静的超脱。

items.en: French apathie carried the word into Western Europe, where doctors began using it for a dull, unresponsive state.
items.cn: 法语 apathie 把这个词带入西欧，医生开始用它指一种呆滞、无反应的状态。

items.en: English took apathy around the 1590s, at first still meaning the philosophical calm the Stoics had praised.
items.cn: 英语在 1590 年代吸收 apathy，起初仍指斯多葛派赞赏的那种哲学式平静。

items.en: By 1733 the word had flipped: writers used apathy for indolence of mind, a failure to care that deserved criticism.
items.cn: 到 1733 年词义翻转：作者们用 apathy 指「心灵的怠惰」，成了该受批评的漠不关心。

note.en: The look-alike group centres on antipathy, which is active dislike rather than no feeling at all; the near-meaning group lists other words for not caring.
note.cn: 形近组的核心是 antipathy：那是主动的反感，而不是完全没有感受；近义组列出其他表示「不在意」的词。

entries.definition: The state of not caring either way.
Sluggish lack of energy and drive.

normalIntro.en: Apathy is a- without plus pathy feeling: the feeling has been taken out, so nothing moves you.
normalIntro.cn: apathy 就是 a-「无」加 pathy「感受」：感受被抽走了，所以什么都打动不了你。

normal.en: It is uncountable: say apathy, not an apathy.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 apathy，不说 an apathy。

normal.en: The adjective is apathetic, with the stress on thetic.
normal.cn: 形容词是 apathetic，重音落在 thetic 上。

normal.en: Antipathy is dislike; apathy is no feeling at all.
normal.cn: antipathy 是反感，apathy 是根本没有感受。

normal.en: Common partners are voter, public and political.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 voter、public 与 political。

normal.en: The opposite pole is enthusiasm or engagement.
normal.cn: 它的反面是 enthusiasm 或 engagement。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where nobody raises a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一场没有人举手的会议。

abstract.en: Imagine a ballot box left almost empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一个几乎空着的投票箱。

abstract.en: Think of a phone ringing in an empty flat.
abstract.cn: 想象空屋里响着却没人接的电话。

examples.en: Apathy is harder to fight than open opposition.
examples.cn: 冷漠比公开的反对更难对付。

examples.en: The campaign tried to shake off decades of voter apathy.
examples.cn: 这场运动试图摆脱数十年的选民冷漠。

examples.en: His apathy towards the project worried the whole team.
examples.cn: 他对项目的漠不关心让全队担忧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「无」+ pathy「感受」——心里没有感受，对什么都提不起劲，就是冷漠 apathy。

root: 希腊语 pathos「受苦、感受」加否定前缀 a-，构成 apatheia「无感」，斯多葛派视之为修养；经拉丁 apathia、法语 apathie 进入英语，词义由「平静超脱」翻转为「冷漠怠惰」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same missing feeling: one person not caring, and a whole crowd not caring about shared matters.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种缺失的感受：一个人不在意，以及一整群人对该共同关心的事不在意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the inner string has gone slack, nothing pulls you
core.cn: 核心意象：心里那根弦松了，对什么都提不起劲

branches.en: A student who will not join any club.
branches.cn: 哪个社团都不肯参加的学生。

branches.en: A shrug instead of an answer.
A polling station with ten visitors.
branches.cn: 一天只来了十个人的投票站。

branches.en: A flood appeal that raises nothing.
branches.cn: 一分钱也没募到的洪灾募捐。

branches.en: Both show feeling that never arrives.
branches.cn: 两者都是那份始终没来的感受。

intro.en: Apathy is built from the Greek prefix a- and the feeling root path-, which also builds sympathy, empathy and antipathy.
intro.cn: apathy 由希腊前缀 a- 与「感受」词根 path- 构成，同一词根还构成 sympathy、empathy 与 antipathy。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Greek pathos and apatheia, passed on through Latin apathia; the prefix family a-/an- is Greek too.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是希腊语 pathos 与 apatheia，经拉丁语 apathia 传来；前缀 a-/an- 也来自希腊语。

latinEntries.exampleCN: pathos 是 apathy 的来源。
apatheia 是斯多葛派的理想。
拉丁语 apathia 传入法语。

definition_zh: n. 猿；类人猿（无尾）；笨拙的模仿者　v. 模仿；照搬（常含贬义）
definition_en: A large tailless primate such as a gorilla or chimpanzee; as a verb, to copy someone's behaviour or style closely and rather clumsily, usually with a hint of criticism.
core_image: 没有尾巴的大猿，以及照着别人动作硬学一遍
scene: 小猩猩照着饲养员的动作把毛巾搭在肩上。The young chimp likes to ape the keeper's gestures.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：动词 ape 指照着别人的样子笨拙模仿，多半带一点贬义。

pos.zh: 猿；类人猿；笨拙的模仿者

derivatives.zh: 像猿一样地；笨拙模仿地

senses.title: A tailless primate
senses.definition: a large primate without a tail, such as a gorilla, chimpanzee, orangutan or gibbon
senses.definitionCN: 没有尾巴的大型灵长类动物，如大猩猩、黑猩猩、红毛猩猩或长臂猿
senses.example: The great apes share most of their DNA with humans.
senses.exampleCN: 类人猿与人类共享大部分 DNA。
senses.why: The key contrast with a monkey is the tail: apes have none, and that single feature is what the noun picks out.
senses.whyCN: 与 monkey 的关键区别在尾巴：猿没有尾巴，这个名词抓住的正是这一条特征。

senses.title: To copy clumsily
senses.definition: to imitate someone's actions, voice or style closely, often without understanding, and usually with a disapproving tone
senses.definitionCN: 紧紧照着他人的动作、声音或风格去模仿，往往并不理解，语气多含贬义
senses.example: The band spent a year aping their heroes before finding a voice.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队照搬偶像整整一年，才找到自己的声音。
senses.why: Apes were long thought to mimic human gestures, so the animal name turned into a verb for shallow copying.
senses.whyCN: 人们长期认为猿会模仿人的动作，于是这个动物名变成了表示浅层照搬的动词。

senses.title: A crude imitator
senses.definition: a person who copies others without originality, or who behaves in a rough, foolish way
senses.definitionCN: 毫无原创性地照搬他人的人，或举止粗鲁愚笨的人
senses.example: He was dismissed as an ape of better painters.
senses.exampleCN: 他被看作只会照搬更优秀画家的人而不受重视。
senses.why: This sense keeps both halves of the word at once: the animal and the copying, aimed at a person as an insult.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项同时保留了词的两半：动物与模仿，用作针对人的贬称。

intro.en: Ape is a native Germanic word, Old English apa, related to Dutch aap and German Affe. The verb sense grew out of the belief that apes mimic people.
intro.cn: ape 是日耳曼本族词，古英语作 apa，与荷兰语 aap、德语 Affe 同源。动词义来自「猿会模仿人」这一观念。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic root is apan-, a word for the large tailless primates known in northern Europe.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼词根是 apan-，指北欧人所知的大型无尾灵长类动物。

items.en: Old English wrote apa for both the animal and, loosely, a fool. The plural was apan.
items.cn: 古英语用 apa 指这种动物，也宽泛地指愚人，复数作 apan。

items.en: Middle English ape kept the animal sense and added the figurative use for someone who copies others.
items.cn: 中古英语 ape 保留动物义，并增加了「照搬他人者」的比喻用法。

items.en: Dutch aap and German Affe are the same word, which shows the term is Germanic rather than borrowed from Latin.
items.cn: 荷兰语 aap 与德语 Affe 是同一个词，说明它是日耳曼词，而非从拉丁语借来。

items.en: Around the 1630s the noun became a verb meaning to mimic, from the popular idea that apes imitate human gestures.
items.cn: 1630 年代前后，名词转动词，意为「模仿」，源自「猿会学人的动作」这一流行观念。

items.en: Modern biology keeps ape for the tailless group, separating it sharply from monkey, which normally has a tail.
items.cn: 现代生物学把 ape 留给无尾类群，与通常有尾的 monkey 明确区分。

note.en: The look-alike group guards against apt and ace, which are only a letter away; the near-meaning group lists verbs for copying.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与只差一个字母的 apt、ace 混淆；近义组列出表示「模仿」的动词。

entries.definition: A top player, or the highest card.
A sleeveless cloak, or a headland.
To copy a voice or manner closely.
entries.definitionCN: 逼真地模仿声音或举止。

entries.definition: To do the same as someone else.
To copy in order to match or beat.

entries.definitionCN: 不动脑子地重复别人的话。

normalIntro.en: Ape has three letters and no tail: apes are the primates that lost the tail, monkeys kept it.
normalIntro.cn: ape 只有三个字母，也没有尾巴：猿是没尾巴的那一类，猴子留着尾巴。

normal.en: Great apes are gorillas, chimps, orangutans and gibbons.
normal.cn: 类人猿包括大猩猩、黑猩猩、红毛猩猩与长臂猿。

normal.en: The verb is disapproving: aping is copying without thought.
normal.cn: 动词含贬义：aping 是不动脑地照搬。

normal.en: Inflections are apes, aped, aping, with no doubled letter.
normal.cn: 变化形式是 apes、aped、aping，不双写字母。

normal.en: Do not confuse ape with apt, which means suitable.
normal.cn: 别把 ape 与 apt「恰当的」混淆。

normal.en: The adjective apish describes foolish imitation.
normal.cn: 形容词 apish 形容愚蠢的模仿。

abstract.en: Picture a chimp copying a keeper's wave.
abstract.cn: 想象黑猩猩学饲养员挥手。

abstract.en: Imagine a band sounding exactly like its heroes.
abstract.cn: 想象一支乐队听起来和偶像一模一样。

abstract.en: Think of a mirror that only repeats, never adds.
abstract.cn: 想象一面只会重复、从不添东西的镜子。

examples.en: Gibbons are the smallest of the apes.
examples.cn: 长臂猿是猿类中体型最小的。

examples.en: He aped his teacher's accent for a laugh.
examples.cn: 他学老师的口音逗大家笑。

examples.en: The film is aping a style it never understands.
examples.cn: 这部电影照搬了一种它并不理解的风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ape 三个字母，尾巴也「没有」——无尾的是 ape，有尾的是 monkey；动词就是照搬别人的动作。

root: 日耳曼本族词，古英语 apa「猿」，与荷兰语 aap、德语 Affe 同源；因古人认为猿善学人动作，1630 年代生出动词「模仿、照搬」，再引申指拙劣的模仿者。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses run from the animal to the copying: a tailless primate, the act of copying like one, and a person who only copies.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从动物走向模仿：无尾的大猿，像猿一样照搬的动作，以及只会照搬的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a big tailless ape, and a clumsy run at someone else's moves
core.cn: 核心意象：没有尾巴的大猿，以及照着别人动作硬学一遍

branches.en: A gorilla with no tail at all.
branches.cn: 完全没有尾巴的大猩猩。

branches.en: A gibbon swinging through the canopy.
branches.cn: 在树冠间摆荡的长臂猿。

branches.en: A chimp copying a keeper's wave.
branches.cn: 学饲养员挥手的小黑猩猩。

branches.en: A painter who only repeats others.

branches.cn: 两者都只是照搬，不加新东西。

intro.en: Ape itself has no affixes, but it takes -ish and -like, and the copying idea is carried by the Latin roots mim- and imit-.
intro.cn: ape 本身不带词缀，但可加 -ish 与 -like；「模仿」这一概念由拉丁词根 mim- 与 imit- 承载。

latinIntro.en: Ape is Germanic, so the classical layer belongs to its synonyms: Latin mimus and imitari, and similis for likeness.
latinIntro.cn: ape 是日耳曼词，所以古典层次属于它的近义词：拉丁语 mimus、imitari，以及表示相似的 similis。

definition_zh: n. 应用程序；手机应用（application 的截短形式）
definition_en: A software application, especially one downloaded to a phone or tablet; the everyday short form of application, now a normal word in its own right.
core_image: 手机屏幕上那一格格点开就用的小图标
scene: 这款应用把整本词典装进了口袋。The app puts the whole dictionary in your pocket.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：app 是 application 的截短，指手机或电脑上的一个应用程序。

senses.title: A software application
senses.definition: a program designed to do a particular job for the user, on any computer or device
senses.definitionCN: 为用户完成某项具体任务的程序，可在任何电脑或设备上运行
senses.example: The desktop app syncs your notes across machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这个桌面应用能在多台设备间同步笔记。
senses.why: App is simply the first syllable of application kept as a whole word, so it covers any application, not only phone ones.
senses.whyCN: app 就是把 application 的第一个音节留下来当整词用，因此它涵盖任何应用程序，不只是手机上的。

senses.title: A phone program you download
senses.definition: in ordinary speech, one of the small icons on a phone screen that you install from a store
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中，指手机屏幕上从应用商店装来的那些小图标之一
senses.example: She deleted three apps to free up space.
senses.exampleCN: 她删了三个应用来腾出空间。
senses.why: After 2008 the store model made this the default meaning, so app now suggests a phone first and a desktop second.
senses.whyCN: 2008 年之后应用商店模式让这层意思成了默认义，如今 app 先让人想到手机，其次才是电脑。

intro.en: App is a clipping of application, which goes back to Latin applicare, to fold towards, from ad- plus plicare, to fold. The short form took off with phone stores.
intro.cn: app 是 application 的截短，而 application 可追到拉丁语 applicare「折向、贴附」，由 ad- 加 plicare「折」构成。这个短形式随手机应用商店流行开来。

items.en: Latin plicare meant to fold. It gives English apply, imply, complicate, reply and explicit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plicare 意为「折叠」。它产生英语的 apply、imply、complicate、reply 与 explicit。

items.en: Adding ad-, to, gave applicare, to fold towards or join to, hence to put one thing onto another.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」得到 applicare「折向、贴附」，因此引申为把一物放到另一物上。

items.en: The noun applicatio meant a joining to, and in later Latin the act of putting something to use.
items.cn: 名词 applicatio 意为「贴附」，在后期拉丁语中指「投入使用」这一动作。

items.en: English took application in the fifteenth century for putting a thing to a purpose, and later for a formal request.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪吸收 application，表示「把某物用于某目的」，后来又指正式申请。

items.en: From the 1960s application named a program written for a user's task, as opposed to system software.
items.cn: 自 1960 年代起，application 指为用户任务编写的程序，与系统软件相对。

items.en: Programmers shortened application to app in the 1980s, and the 2008 phone stores made it an everyday word.
items.cn: 1980 年代程序员把 application 缩为 app，2008 年的手机应用商店让它成为日常词。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against apt and ape, which differ by one letter; the near-meaning group gives the fuller words for the same thing.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与只差一个字母的 apt、ape 混淆；近义组给出指同一事物的更完整说法。

entries.definition: A round fruit; also a tech brand.
entries.definitionCN: 一种圆形水果；也指一个科技品牌。

entries.definition: A set of instructions a computer runs.
entries.definitionCN: 计算机执行的一组指令。

entries.definition: A small utility that does one job.

normalIntro.en: App is application cut down to its first three letters, the part you say anyway when speaking fast.
normalIntro.cn: app 就是 application 砍到只剩前三个字母，也就是你说快时本来只会念出的那一截。

normal.en: It is countable: one app, two apps.
normal.cn: 它可数：one app、two apps。

normal.en: Write app in lower case unless it starts a sentence.
normal.cn: 除句首外，app 一律小写。

normal.en: The full form application is still used in formal writing.
normal.cn: 正式书面语仍用完整形式 application。

normal.en: Do not confuse app with apt, which means suitable.
normal.cn: 别把 app 与 apt「恰当的」混淆。

normal.en: App store, app icon and app developer are fixed pairs.
normal.cn: app store、app icon、app developer 都是固定搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a grid of icons waiting for a tap.
abstract.cn: 想象一屏等着被点开的图标。

abstract.en: Imagine a long word trimmed to its first syllable.
abstract.cn: 想象一个长词被剪到只剩第一个音节。

abstract.en: Think of a whole dictionary folded into a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象整本词典被折进口袋。

examples.en: The app works offline once the words are downloaded.
examples.cn: 单词下载好之后，这个应用可以离线使用。

examples.en: He builds apps for small museums.
examples.cn: 他为小型博物馆开发应用。

examples.en: Delete the apps you have not opened in a month.
examples.cn: 把一个月没打开过的应用删掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：application 掐掉后半截，只留前三个字母 app——手机上一格图标就是一个 app。

root: 拉丁语 plicare「折」加 ad-「向」成 applicare「贴附」，名词 applicatio 经法语进入英语作 application「运用、申请」；计算机时代指应用程序，1980 年代截短为 app。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one clipped word: any application on any device, and the phone application that the word now suggests first.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个截短词：任何设备上的任何应用程序，以及如今这个词最先让人想到的手机应用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the little grid of icons you tap open on a screen
core.cn: 核心意象：手机屏幕上那一格格点开就用的小图标

branches.en: A desktop program that syncs notes.
A tool that converts one file to another.
branches.cn: 把一种文件转成另一种的工具。

branches.en: An icon installed from a store.
branches.cn: 从商店装来的一个图标。

branches.en: Three apps deleted to free space.
branches.cn: 为腾空间删掉的三个应用。
两者都是 application 的截短。

intro.en: App hides the prefix ap- and the fold root plic-, which build apply, application, applicant, appliance and applicable.
intro.cn: app 里藏着前缀 ap- 与「折」词根 plic-，它们构成 apply、application、applicant、appliance 与 applicable。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is plicare, to fold, applicare, to fold towards, and the noun applicatio, a joining to.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 plicare「折」、applicare「折向」，以及名词 applicatio「贴附」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: plicare 是 apply 的来源。

definition_zh: 使惊骇；使震惊；使胆寒
definition_en: to fill someone with horror or shock
core_image: 推开房门后猛地倒吸的一口冷气
scene: 老屋的门被推开，尘土里露出塌了半边的地板。The condition of the house appalled the inspectors.
sceneCN: 这里 appall 是「使惊骇」（第 1 个义项：令人极度震惊恐惧）；句意为房屋的状况令检查人员大为震惊。

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转形容词，义为「骇人的；糟糕透顶的」
由 appalling 加 -ly 构成，义为「骇人地；极糟地」
同根词，义为「（棺）罩；（使）失去吸引力」

senses.title: To fill with horror
senses.definition: to shock and horrify someone deeply
senses.definitionCN: 使某人深感震惊与恐惧
senses.example: The condition of the house appalled the inspectors.
senses.exampleCN: 房屋的状况令检查人员大为震惊。
senses.why: The old image is a pall, the dark cloth thrown over a face or coffin: horror as something laid over you like a shroud.
senses.whyCN: 古老的意象是 pall——盖在面孔或棺木上的黑布：惊骇就像一块裹尸布罩到你身上。

senses.title: To grow pale with fear
senses.definition: to turn pale or weak with dread, the older intransitive use
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧而脸色发白、浑身无力，为较早期的用法
senses.example: Her cheeks appalled at the dreadful news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到噩耗，她的双颊吓得发白。
senses.why: Pall means to grow pale, so to appall was first to blanch someone's face with fear.
senses.whyCN: pall 本指变得苍白，所以 appall 最初指吓得人脸色发白。

intro.en: Appall combines the prefix ap- (ad-, 'to') with pall, from Old English paell, a cloak or covering.
intro.cn: appall 由前缀 ap-（ad-「朝向」）加 pall 构成，pall 来自古英语 paell「斗篷；罩布」。

items.en: paell meant a rich cloak or covering cloth.
items.cn: 古英语 paell 指华贵的斗篷或罩布。

items.en: pall named the cloth draped over coffins and chalices.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 pall 指覆盖棺木与圣杯的罩布。

items.en: The verb pall meant 'to cloak' and then 'to grow pale or tiresome'.
items.cn: 动词 pall 先指「披罩」，后指「变得苍白或令人厌倦」。

items.en: Middle English formed appallen, 'to grow pale with horror'.
items.cn: 中古英语构成 appallen「吓得脸色发白」。

items.en: Today the transitive sense dominates: to appall someone; the adjective appalling is the commonest form.
items.cn: 如今及物义占主导：使某人惊骇；形容词 appalling 最为常用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pall family; the near-meaning group gathers words of horror.
note.cn: 形近组收 pall 词族；近义组收表示「惊骇」的词。

entries.definition: a coffin cloth; to become dull or tiresome
entries.definitionCN: 棺罩；（乐趣）衰减，本词的同根词
苍白的；与拉丁 pallere「苍白」相关，词义呼应
呼吁；吸引力；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to fill with worry and disappointment
entries.definitionCN: 使惊愕；使沮丧，惊中带愁

normalIntro.en: Appall throws a dark pall over the mind.
normalIntro.cn: appall 就像往心头罩一块黑布。

normal.en: ap- (to) + pall (cover) = throw a cover over.
normal.cn: ap-（朝向）加 pall（罩布），即「罩住」。

normal.en: Two l's in American spelling: appall, appalling.
normal.cn: 美式拼写双写 l：appall、appalling。

normal.en: Appalling is far more common than the verb.
normal.cn: appalling 比动词原形常用得多。

normal.en: Be appalled at/by is the standard pattern.
normal.cn: 标准搭配是 be appalled at/by。

normal.en: Pall as a verb means the pleasure fades.
normal.cn: pall 作动词指兴致渐消。

abstract.en: See a black cloth dropped over a cage.
abstract.cn: 想象黑布罩住鸟笼。

abstract.en: See a face draining of colour.
abstract.cn: 想象脸色一寸寸变白。

abstract.en: See a door opening onto wreckage.
abstract.cn: 想象推门见到一片狼藉。

examples.en: The condition of the house appalled the inspectors.
examples.cn: 房屋的状况令检查人员大为震惊。

examples.en: Her cheeks appalled at the dreadful news.
examples.cn: 听到噩耗，她的双颊吓得发白。

examples.en: They were appalled by the waste of food.
examples.cn: 他们对食物的浪费感到震惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄怕」——「厄」运临头，「怕」得脸色发白，正是惊骇之态。

root: 中古英语 appallen「吓得发白」，由前缀 ap-（ad-「朝向」）+ pall「罩布、棺衣」（古英语 paell「斗篷」）构成；比喻惊骇如黑布罩身。

sensesIntro.en: From a covering cloth came paling cheeks, then deep horror.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一块罩布，到吓得发白的脸颊，再到深深的惊骇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shroud thrown over the face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块裹尸布罩上面孔。

intro.en: An English verb of covering, built with the Latin-looking prefix ad-.
intro.cn: 一个表示「罩住」的英语动词，配上前缀 ad-。

latinIntro.en: The pall- family in English mixes the cloth word and Latin pallor.
latinIntro.cn: 英语 pall- 词族混合了罩布义与拉丁语的苍白义。

definition_zh: 为特定用途配置的一整套器械或装置；也可指机构、组织等抽象体系
definition_en: a set of equipment assembled for a particular purpose, or an organized system such as a state or party structure
core_image: 实验台上，玻璃管、支架、气瓶与阀门连成一套，每一段都扣在指定的位置，只为完成一次反应
scene: 潜水前，队员检查背上的气瓶、减压阀与面罩，确认每一处接头都不漏气。The diver checked the breathing apparatus before the descent.
sceneCN: 这里指成套的呼吸装置（第 2 个义项：为潜水或消防配置的呼吸器）；句意：潜水员在下潜前检查了呼吸装置。

derivatives.zh: 由「装置」加英语复数词尾构成，义为「多套装置」
由拉丁语「预先准备」经法语进入英语，义为「准备」
由「准备」加名词词尾构成，义为「准备、制备」
由「准备」加形容词词尾构成，义为「预备的」
由拉丁语「重新准备」经法语进入英语，义为「修理」

senses.title: A set assembled for an experiment
senses.titleCN: 为实验组装的一套器械
senses.definition: the connected pieces of equipment set up to carry out a particular experiment or operation
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某项实验或操作而连接起来的一套器材
senses.example: The whole apparatus was rebuilt after the glass tube broke.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃管破裂后，整套装置被重新组装。
senses.why: Apparatus names a prepared set, not a single tool, because its root verb means to make ready.
senses.whyCN: 「装置」指准备好的一套，而不是单件工具，因为其词根动词意为「准备」。

senses.title: Breathing gear
senses.definition: the cylinder, regulator and mask that let a person breathe under water, in smoke or at altitude
senses.definitionCN: 让人在水下、烟雾中或高空呼吸的气瓶、调节器与面罩组合
senses.example: Firefighters carry breathing apparatus into every smoke-filled room.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员进入每个烟雾弥漫的房间都携带呼吸器。
senses.why: A life-support set is prepared before entry, so the general word attaches to this specialised kit.
senses.whyCN: 生命维持装备要在进入前准备好，因此这个泛称也附着于这套专用器材。

senses.title: The machinery of an organization
senses.definition: the offices, departments and procedures through which a state, party or large body acts
senses.definitionCN: 国家、政党或大型团体赖以行动的机关、部门与程序
senses.example: The reform aimed at the party apparatus rather than at voters.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革针对的是政党机构，而不是选民。
senses.why: An organisation acts through prepared parts, so the tool word becomes a metaphor for institutional machinery.
senses.whyCN: 组织通过准备好的各个部件行动，于是工具词变成了机构机械的比喻。

senses.title: Gymnastic equipment
senses.definition: the fixed or portable frames and bars used in gymnastics, such as the rings or parallel bars
senses.definitionCN: 体操中使用的固定或可移动框架与横杆，如吊环或双杠
senses.example: The hall's apparatus was inspected before the competition.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前，馆内的体操器械接受了检查。
senses.why: Sporting equipment is also a prepared set, so the word serves for bars, rings and beams.
senses.whyCN: 运动器材同样是准备好的一套，因此这个词也用于横杆、吊环与平衡木。

senses.title: Optical or measuring setup
senses.definition: a bench of lenses, mirrors, lasers and detectors aligned for one measurement
senses.definitionCN: 为一次测量而对准的透镜、反射镜、激光器与探测器组合
senses.example: The optical apparatus had to stay aligned within a micron.
senses.exampleCN: 这套光学装置必须在微米范围内保持对准。
senses.why: Precision work needs many parts fixed in relation to one another, which is exactly what apparatus means.
senses.whyCN: 精密工作需要许多部件按相对位置固定，这正是「装置」所指。

senses.title: Textual collation notes
senses.definition: the recorded variants and editorial notes that accompany a scholarly edition of a text
senses.definitionCN: 学术版本正文旁记录的异文与编者说明
senses.example: The critical apparatus lists every manuscript reading.
senses.exampleCN: 校勘资料列出了每种抄本的读法。
senses.why: Scholars prepare a text with supporting parts, and the old word for equipment names those supporting notes.
senses.whyCN: 学者为正文准备支撑材料，古老的「装备」一词便用来指这些辅助记录。

senses.title: The assembly of a machine
senses.definition: the connected parts of a machine considered as one working whole
senses.definitionCN: 把一台机器的各连接部件视为一个运作整体
senses.example: The valve is only one part of the pumping apparatus.
senses.exampleCN: 阀门只是泵送装置的一部分。
senses.why: The word can name the whole working assembly, not only a bench setup, whenever the parts act together.
senses.whyCN: 只要部件协同运作，这个词就可指整个工作总成，而不只是台面装置。

senses.title: Darkroom and photographic gear
senses.definition: the enlarger, trays, tanks and safelights used to develop photographs
senses.definitionCN: 用于冲洗照片的放大机、药盘、罐与安全灯
senses.example: The school still keeps a darkroom apparatus behind the studio.
senses.exampleCN: 学校仍在摄影室后面保留着一套暗房器材。
senses.why: A craft that needs a fixed sequence of prepared tools give the word another specialised home.
senses.whyCN: 需要固定工序与预备工具的技艺，又给这个词添了一个专用场所。

intro.en: Apparatus is a Latin noun for equipment, built on a verb meaning to prepare; English borrowed it whole, including its Latin plural.
intro.cn: 「装置」是拉丁语中表示装备的名词，建立在表示「准备」的动词上；英语整体借入，连拉丁语复数形式也一并保留。

items.en: Parare meant to prepare, make ready or furnish; it is the direct Latin source, while its deeper origin is uncertain and the link to a producing root is only a suggestion.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语动词指准备、备好或供给；它是本词的直接拉丁语来源，其更早来源存疑，与表示「产出」之古词根的关联仅为推测。

items.en: The prefix ad-, meaning toward, combined with parare to give apparare, to get ready for a purpose.
items.cn: 表示「朝向」的前缀与「准备」结合，构成「为某目的做好准备」的动词。

items.en: Apparatus was the result noun: the state of being prepared and the set of things prepared, especially for a task.
items.cn: 这个词是结果名词，指准备好的状态以及准备好的一套东西，尤指为某项任务所备。

items.en: The Latin fourth-declension noun kept the same form in the plural, and English still allows apparatus as a plural.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语第四变格名词的复数与原形同形，英语至今仍允许用原形作复数。

items.era: ENGLISH BORROWING · FIRST RECORD DATE UNCERTAIN
items.en: English took the word in the seventeenth century for a prepared set of instruments, especially in science; the exact year of the borrowing is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个词，指准备好的一套器具，尤用于科学；具体借入年代不确定。

items.en: The same picture of prepared parts was later applied to state and party machinery and to the notes that support an edited text.
items.cn: 同一幅「准备好的部件」画面后来被用于国家与政党机构，以及支撑校勘版本的注释。

note.en: The first group shares the prepare root; the second group separates the four kit words.
note.cn: 第一组共享「准备」词根；第二组区分四个器械名词。

entries.definition: The English plural, used when several separate sets are counted.
entries.definitionCN: 英语复数，用于清点几套分开的装置。

entries.definition: To make ready; the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 做好准备；名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: The act of making ready; it stresses the process, not the set.
entries.definitionCN: 准备的动作；强调过程而非成套之物。

entries.definition: To make ready again; it shares the prepare root with a again-prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 重新备好；共享「准备」词根并带「再次」前缀。

entries.definition: A bought or issued set of machines and tools; apparatus is assembled for a task.
entries.definitionCN: 采购或配发的成套机器工具；装置是为任务组装起来的。

entries.definition: One precision measuring tool; apparatus is the whole setup around it.
entries.definitionCN: 单件精密测量器具；装置是围绕它的整套布置。

entries.definition: The installed system of measuring and control devices in a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 工厂中安装的测量与控制仪表系统。

entries.definition: An improvised or temporary setup; apparatus is more deliberate and complete.
entries.definitionCN: 临时拼搭的装置；目标词更像有意搭成的完整一套。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real fixed terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root verb means to prepare, so apparatus is the set made ready.
normal.cn: 词根动词意为准备，因此装置就是准备好的一套。

normal.en: The family runs prepare, preparation, preparatory, repair and apparatus.
normal.cn: 同族词包括准备、制备、预备的、修理与装置。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: laboratory apparatus, breathing apparatus, state apparatus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配可标记它：实验装置、呼吸器、国家机构。

normal.en: The Latin plural is the same word, though English also allows apparatuses.
normal.cn: 拉丁语复数与原形同形，英语也允许加复数词尾。

normal.en: Its cousins are equipment, instrument, instrumentation and rig.
normal.cn: 它的近亲是设备、仪器、仪表系统与临时装置。

abstract.en: Picture a table where every glass tube knows exactly where it belongs.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，每根玻璃管都清楚自己该在哪里。

abstract.en: Picture a mask that turns a hostile environment into breathable air.
abstract.cn: 想象一副面罩，把恶劣环境变成可呼吸的空气。

abstract.en: Picture a building full of offices acting like one prepared machine.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋装满办公室的建筑，像一台准备好的机器那样运作。

examples.en: The apparatus must be assembled in the order given in the manual.
examples.cn: 这套装置必须按手册给定的顺序组装。

examples.en: The state apparatus moved faster than the ministry itself.
examples.cn: 国家机构比部委本身行动得更快。

examples.en: A broken seal can ruin an entire breathing apparatus.
examples.cn: 一处密封破损就能毁掉整套呼吸装置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「预先备好」的一整套器械，连复数都沿用拉丁原形

root: 源自拉丁语「为某目的准备」的动词及其结果名词；更早词源不确定，英语十七世纪整体借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: parts prepared and joined for a purpose. The purpose may be an experiment, breathing, sport, measurement, scholarship or the action of an organization.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个观念：部件为某目的备好并连接起来。这个目的可以是实验、呼吸、运动、测量、校勘，或一个组织的行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bench of parts clipped into place, each in its fixed position, ready for one operation.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台面部件被扣在各自固定位置，为一套操作准备就绪。

branches.en: THE CORE: an assembled set for an experiment, and the working parts of a machine.
branches.cn: 核心：为实验组装的整套器械，以及机器的工作部件。

branches.en: THE LIFE-SUPPORT VERSION: cylinders, regulators and masks.
branches.cn: 生命维持版本：气瓶、调节器与面罩。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTIONAL VERSION: the offices and procedures of a state or party.
branches.cn: 机构版本：国家或政党的机关与程序。

branches.en: THE SPORT AND DARKROOM VERSION: rings, bars, enlargers and trays.
branches.cn: 运动与暗房版本：吊环、横杆、放大机与药盘。

branches.en: THE PRECISION AND SCHOLARLY VERSION: aligned optical benches and collation notes.
branches.cn: 精密与学术版本：对准的光学台与校勘注释。

intro.en: The word is wholly Latin: a preparing verb, a purpose prefix and a result noun.
intro.cn: 这个词完全来自拉丁语：一个「准备」动词、一个表目的前缀与一个结果名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin apparare and apparatus supply the form; the plural is the same Latin form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「准备」与「装置」提供了词形；复数沿用同一拉丁形式。

items.example: The base verb of the family.

items.exampleCN: 在辅音前变为另一形式。

items.meaning: to get ready for a purpose

items.example: It forms apparatuses beside the Latin plural.
items.exampleCN: 它与拉丁复数并存构成英语复数。

The again-prefix plus the prepare root.

definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；表面上的
definition_en: easy to see or understand, or seeming true without being so
core_image: 水面上露出的冰山一角
scene: 会议室的空气一下子僵住，谁都看得出出了问题。It was apparent that something had gone wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 apparent 是「明显的」（第 1 个义项：容易看出来）；句意是显然出了什么问题。

pos.zh: 形容词：明显的；表面上的

senses.title: Clearly visible or understood
senses.definition: easy to notice or understand from the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 根据证据很容易被察觉或理解
senses.example: It was apparent that something had gone wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 显然出了什么问题。
senses.why: Latin apparere meant 'to come into view', built from ad, 'to', and parere, 'to appear'; what is apparent has come into sight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 apparere 意为「进入视野」，由 ad「向」与 parere「出现」构成；apparent 就是已经进入视线的东西。

senses.title: Seeming rather than real
senses.definition: true as far as one can see, but possibly not in fact
senses.definitionCN: 就所见而言成立，但事实上未必如此
senses.example: The apparent calm hid a great deal of anger.
senses.exampleCN: 表面上的平静掩藏着极大的愤怒。
senses.why: Because appearing is not the same as being, apparent can warn that the surface may deceive.
senses.whyCN: 因为「显现」不等于「实有」，所以 apparent 可以提醒表面可能欺人。

intro.en: Apparent comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to come into view'.
intro.cn: apparent 来自拉丁语中意为「进入视野」的动词。

items.en: ad meant 'to, towards'.
items.cn: ad 意为「向、朝」。

items.en: parere meant 'to appear, come forth'.

definition_zh: 呼吁；恳求；上诉；吸引力；吸引
definition_en: to make an urgent request, to ask a court to change a decision, or to be attractive to someone

scene: 洪水过后，村长站在废墟前向外界求援。The village appealed for food and clean water.
sceneCN: 这里 appeal 是「呼吁；恳求」（第 1 个义项：紧急请求帮助）；句意是村里呼吁提供食物和干净的水。

senses.title: To ask urgently for help
senses.definition: to ask strongly and publicly for something needed
senses.definitionCN: 公开而强烈地请求所需之物
senses.example: The village appealed for food and clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 村里呼吁提供食物和干净的水。
senses.why: Latin appellare meant 'to address, call upon', from ad, 'to', and pellere, 'to drive'; an appeal drives words toward someone who can act.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appellare 意为「向……讲话、呼唤」，由 ad「向」与 pellere「推动」构成；appeal 就是把话推向能行动的人。

senses.title: To ask a court to reconsider
senses.definition: to take a legal decision to a higher court for review
senses.definitionCN: 把法律裁决提交上级法院复审
senses.example: They appealed against the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对判决提出上诉。
senses.why: The idea of calling upon a higher authority fits the courtroom: the losing side calls on a higher court.
senses.whyCN: 「向更高权威求助」的观念正适用于法庭：败诉一方向更高一级法院发出请求。

senses.title: To be attractive
senses.definition: to please or interest someone, often because it suits their needs

senses.example: The simple design appeals to young buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 简洁的设计吸引了年轻买家。
senses.why: Something that appeals to you calls out to your taste, so the word moved from a spoken request to a silent attraction.
senses.whyCN: appeal to 你的东西是在向你的品味发出呼唤，所以这个词从口头请求延伸为无声的吸引。

definition_zh: 出现；露面；显得；出庭
definition_en: to come into sight, to seem a certain way, or to be present in public or in court
core_image: 舞台幕布拉开，演员走到灯光下
scene: 观众等了几秒，幕布一开，主角从侧幕走出来。A figure appeared at the end of the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里 appear 是「出现」（第 1 个义项：进入视线）；句意是一个身影出现在走廊尽头。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：明显的；表面上的

senses.title: To come into sight
senses.definition: to become visible or present where someone can see you
senses.definitionCN: 变得可见，或出现在别人能看到的地方
senses.example: A figure appeared at the end of the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 一个身影出现在走廊尽头。
senses.why: Latin apparere joined ad, 'to', and parere, 'to come forth', so appear is a thing stepping into view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 apparere 由 ad「向」与 parere「出现」合成，所以 appear 就是某物走进视野。

senses.title: To seem a certain way
senses.definition: to give a particular impression, often without being so in fact
senses.definitionCN: 给人某种印象，而事实上未必如此
senses.example: The task appears easier than it is.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任务看起来比实际容易。
senses.why: What steps into view is what we judge by, so appear came to mean 'look like' rather than simply 'be present'.
senses.whyCN: 走进视野的东西正是我们判断的依据，所以 appear 从「在场」转为「看起来像」。

senses.title: To be present officially
senses.definition: to attend a court, a hearing, or a public event as required
senses.definitionCN: 按要求出席法庭、听证会或公开活动
senses.example: He must appear before the judge on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 他必须在周一出庭面见法官。
senses.why: A court requires the person to show themselves in the room, which is the plainest form of appearing.
senses.whyCN: 法庭要求当事人亲自出现在庭上，这正是 appear 最朴素的形态。

sensesIntro.en: The event of showing up, the look produced by it, and the required court presence.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person checked over in a mirror before entering.
core.cn: 核心意象：进门之前在镜前检视自己的人。

intro.en: A regular noun of the appear family, very productive in English.
intro.cn: 这是 appear 词族中的规则名词，在英语中构词力很强。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root parere, 'to appear', runs through the family.

definition_zh: n. 阑尾炎（阑尾的炎症，急性发作常需手术切除）
definition_en: Inflammation of the appendix, the small pouch hanging off the large intestine; an acute attack causes worsening pain in the lower right abdomen and usually needs surgery.
core_image: 右下腹那一点突然绞紧，按下去更疼
scene: 半夜右下腹剧痛，急诊确诊为急性阑尾炎。Acute appendicitis sent him to the operating theatre before dawn.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：appendicitis 指阑尾发炎，典型表现是右下腹持续加重的疼痛。

senses.title: Inflammation of the appendix
senses.definition: the medical condition in which the appendix becomes swollen and infected, named by the suffix -itis
senses.definitionCN: 阑尾肿胀发炎的病症，由后缀 -itis 标明为炎症
senses.example: Appendicitis is one of the commonest causes of abdominal surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 阑尾炎是腹部手术最常见的病因之一。
senses.why: The word is appendix plus -itis, so it names the disease by naming the part and then marking it as inflamed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 appendix 加 -itis，先点出部位，再标上「发炎」，病名就这样拼出来了。

senses.title: A surgical emergency
senses.definition: used of an acute attack that must be treated quickly, before the appendix bursts and infects the abdomen
senses.definitionCN: 指必须在阑尾穿孔感染腹腔之前尽快处理的急性发作
senses.example: The surgeon treated it as appendicitis and operated within two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生按阑尾炎处理，两小时内就动了手术。
senses.why: In hospital speech the word carries urgency: saying appendicitis is not just naming a disease but calling for an operation.
senses.whyCN: 在医院语境里这个词带着紧迫感：说 appendicitis 不只是报病名，而是在要求立刻手术。

intro.en: Appendicitis is appendix plus the inflammation suffix -itis. Appendix comes from Latin appendere, to hang beside, from ad- and pendere, to hang.
intro.cn: appendicitis 是 appendix 加炎症后缀 -itis。appendix 来自拉丁语 appendere「挂在旁边」，由 ad- 与 pendere「悬挂」构成。

items.en: Latin pendere meant to hang, and also to weigh, since scales hang. It gives pendant, pendulum, depend and suspend.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 意为「悬挂」，也指「称重」，因为天平是挂着的。它产生 pendant、pendulum、depend 与 suspend。

items.en: With ad-, to, it became appendere, to hang something beside a main thing, so the added part is secondary.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」成为 appendere「把某物挂在主体旁边」，因此附加的部分是次要的。

items.en: The noun appendix meant an appendage, and English used it for a supplement at the end of a book.
items.cn: 名词 appendix 意为「附属物」，英语用它指书末的附录。

items.en: Anatomy kept appendix for the small blind pouch hanging off the caecum, a literal appendage of the gut.
items.cn: 解剖学把 appendix 留给挂在盲肠上的那条小盲管，它字面上就是肠子的附属物。

items.en: Greek -itis was a feminine adjective ending agreeing with nosos, disease; medicine reanalysed it as inflammation.
items.cn: 希腊语 -itis 本是与 nosos「疾病」呼应的阴性形容词词尾，医学把它重新理解为「炎症」。

items.en: Reginald Fitz named the condition appendicitis in 1886 and argued for early surgery, which saved many lives.
items.cn: 1886 年 Reginald Fitz 把这一病症命名为 appendicitis，并主张早期手术，救了许多人的命。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the organ appendix from the disease, and shows other -itis names; the near-meaning group lists related abdominal conditions.
note.cn: 形近组把器官 appendix 与疾病区分开，并展示其他 -itis 病名；近义组列出相关的腹部病症。

entries.definition: The pouch itself, or a book supplement.
Swelling, heat and pain in tissue.
Sharp gripping pain in the belly.
Invasion by germs that harm tissue.

normalIntro.en: Appendicitis is appendix plus -itis: the little hanging pouch has become inflamed.
normalIntro.cn: appendicitis 就是 appendix 加 -itis：那条挂着的小盲管发炎了。

normal.en: The suffix -itis always marks inflammation.
normal.cn: 后缀 -itis 一律表示炎症。

normal.en: Appendix is the part; appendicitis is the disease.
normal.cn: appendix 是部位，appendicitis 是疾病。

normal.en: It is uncountable: say appendicitis, not an appendicitis.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 appendicitis，不说 an appendicitis。

normal.en: The stress falls on -ci-, /ˈsaɪ/, not on the start.
normal.cn: 重音落在 -ci- 上，读 /ˈsaɪ/，不在词首。

normal.en: The operation is an appendectomy, with -ectomy for removal.
normal.cn: 手术叫 appendectomy，-ectomy 表示切除。

abstract.en: Picture a small pouch swelling on the side of a pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象管道侧面一个小囊袋肿了起来。

abstract.en: Imagine pain moving from the navel to the lower right.
abstract.cn: 想象疼痛从肚脐移到右下腹。

abstract.en: Think of a clock: every hour of delay raises the risk.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟：每延误一小时，风险就升一分。

examples.en: The doctor ruled out appendicitis after a scan.
examples.cn: 扫描之后，医生排除了阑尾炎。

examples.en: Untreated appendicitis can lead to peritonitis.
examples.cn: 阑尾炎不治疗可能引发腹膜炎。

examples.en: She was in hospital for a week after appendicitis.
examples.cn: 阑尾炎之后她住院一周。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：append「附加」+ ix + itis「炎」——挂在肠子旁边那截小尾巴发炎了，就是阑尾炎 appendicitis。

root: 拉丁语 pendere「悬挂」加 ad-「向」成 appendere「挂在旁边」，名词 appendix「附属物」被解剖学用来指阑尾；再加希腊炎症后缀 -itis，1886 年构成病名 appendicitis。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one inflamed pouch: the disease as a named condition, and the same disease as an emergency that must be operated on.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一条发炎的盲管：作为病名的疾病，以及作为必须立刻手术的急症的同一疾病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one spot in the lower right belly gripping tight, worse when pressed
core.cn: 核心意象：右下腹那一点突然绞紧，按下去更疼

branches.en: A pouch swollen beside the gut.
branches.cn: 肠子旁边肿起来的盲管。

branches.en: A named cause of belly surgery.
branches.cn: 腹部手术的一个明确病因。

branches.en: Pain shifting to the lower right.
Surgery within two hours of arrival.
Both are the same inflamed appendage.
branches.cn: 两者都是同一条发炎的附属盲管。

intro.en: Appendicitis joins the prefix ap-, the hang root pend- and the disease suffix -itis, a pattern shared by many medical names.
intro.cn: appendicitis 拼合了前缀 ap-、「悬挂」词根 pend- 与疾病后缀 -itis，这是许多医学病名共用的构词模式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is pendere, appendere and appendix; the suffix -itis is Greek but arrived through medical Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 pendere、appendere 与 appendix；后缀 -itis 来自希腊语，但经医学拉丁语传入。

latinEntries.exampleCN: pendere 产生 pendant 与 depend。
appendix 被用来命名肠道盲管。
itis 把 arthritis 标为炎症。

definition_zh: 食欲；胃口；欲望；兴趣
definition_en: a natural desire for food, or a strong interest in something
core_image: 闻到厨房香味时咽下的口水
scene: 锅盖一掀，热气冲上脸，他立刻觉得饿了。The smell of bread gave him an appetite.
sceneCN: 这里 appetite 是「食欲」（第 1 个义项：对食物的自然欲望）；句意是面包的香味让他有了食欲。

senses.title: A desire for food
senses.definition: the natural feeling that makes you want to eat
senses.definitionCN: 使人想吃东西的自然感觉
senses.example: The smell of bread gave him an appetite.
senses.exampleCN: 面包的香味让他有了食欲。
senses.why: Latin appetitus came from appetere, 'to seek after', built from ad, 'to', and petere, 'to seek'; hunger is the body seeking food.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appetitus 来自 appetere「追寻」，由 ad「向」与 petere「寻求」构成；饥饿就是身体在追寻食物。

senses.title: A strong interest in something
senses.definition: a keen desire for an activity, a challenge, or a type of experience
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动、挑战或某种体验的强烈渴望
senses.example: She has an appetite for risk.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜欢冒险。
senses.why: The seeking after food widened to any object the mind reaches for, so appetite can name ambition or curiosity.
senses.whyCN: 对食物的追寻扩展到心里想抓取的任何对象，所以 appetite 也能指抱负或好奇心。

intro.en: Appetite goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to seek after'.
intro.cn: appetite 可追溯到拉丁语中意为「追寻」的动词。

items.en: ad meant 'to, towards'.
items.cn: ad 意为「向」。

items.en: petere meant 'to seek, aim at'.
items.cn: petere 意为「寻求、瞄准」。

items.en: appetere meant 'to reach for, desire'.
items.cn: appetere 意为「伸手去取、渴望」。

items.en: Old French brought the noun into English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带入英语。

items.en: The figurative sense of desiring challenges or knowledge became common.
items.cn: 渴望挑战或知识的比喻义变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the seek root; the near-meaning group gives other words for desire.
note.cn: 形近组共享「寻求」词根；近义组是其他表示欲望的词。

entries.definition: a small dish before a meal
a contest, from the same seeking verb

normalIntro.en: Appetite is the body or mind reaching out for something.
normalIntro.cn: appetite 就是身体或心思向外伸出去抓某样东西。

normal.en: Lose one's appetite and a good appetite are opposite fixed pairs.
normal.cn: lose one's appetite 与 a good appetite 是相反的两个固定搭配。

normal.en: An appetite for risk means a taste for it.
normal.cn: an appetite for risk 意为喜欢冒险。

normal.en: Whet one's appetite means make someone want more.
normal.cn: whet one's appetite 意为吊起胃口。

normal.en: Appetizer is the small dish that starts a meal.
normal.cn: appetizer 是开胃的头盘。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AP-pe-tite.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AP-pe-tite。

abstract.en: See steam rising from a covered pot.
abstract.cn: 想象锅盖下冒出的热气。

abstract.en: See a hand reach toward a bread basket.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向面包篮。

abstract.en: See a climber eyeing a high wall.
abstract.cn: 想象攀爬者盯着高墙。

examples.en: The smell of bread gave him an appetite.
examples.cn: 面包的香味让他有了食欲。

examples.en: She has an appetite for risk.
examples.cn: 她喜欢冒险。

examples.en: He lost his appetite after the long journey.
examples.cn: 长途旅行之后他没了胃口。

dict_mnemonic.text: ap-（向）加 pet（寻求）加 -ite：向食物伸出去的欲望，食欲。

root: 来自拉丁语 appetitus，源于 appetere「追寻」，由 ad「向」与 petere「寻求」构成；同根词有 appetizing、appetizer，另有 compete、petition。

sensesIntro.en: Seeking food and seeking experience are the same reaching motion.
sensesIntro.cn: 追寻食物与追寻体验，是同一个向外伸手的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand moving toward food before the mind decides.
core.cn: 核心意象：手在脑子决定之前已伸向食物。

intro.en: A Latin noun of seeking that English applies to food and to ambition.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示追寻的拉丁名词，英语中兼指食物与抱负。

latinIntro.en: The root petere, 'to seek', also gives petition and compete.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 petere「寻求」也派生出 petition 与 compete。

definition_zh: 鼓掌；喝彩；称赞；赞许
definition_en: to show approval by clapping the hands, or to praise a person, action, or idea
core_image: 双手拍在一起的声音：用掌声把喜欢和赞成表达出来
scene: 演出结束，观众纷纷起身。The audience stood up to applaud the pianist after her final piece.
sceneCN: 这里 applaud 是「鼓掌；喝彩」（第 1 个义项：拍手表示赞赏）；句意为「钢琴家弹完最后一曲后，观众起身为她鼓掌」。这个词既可以指真实的拍手动作，也可以引申为口头或态度上的称赞。

pos.zh: 称赞；赞许（某人、某行为或某决定）

derivatives.zh: applaud 加名词后缀 -se 构成，义为「鼓掌；掌声；喝彩」
applaud 加施动者后缀 -er 构成，义为「鼓掌者；称赞者」
applaud 加形容词后缀 -able 的少见变体，义为「值得称赞的」，更常用 plausible 之外的形式 praiseworthy 表达

senses.title: To clap the hands to show enjoyment
senses.definition: to hit your hands together repeatedly to show that you enjoyed a performance
senses.definitionCN: 反复拍手，表示欣赏演出或表演
senses.example: The audience applauded loudly at the end of the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会结束时，观众热烈鼓掌。
senses.why: The core image is hands coming together to make sound; the most direct use is the physical clap itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是双手相击发出声响；最直接的用法就是拍手这个物理动作本身。

senses.title: To clap to welcome or thank someone
senses.definition: to clap in order to welcome a person onto a stage or to thank them
senses.definitionCN: 以掌声欢迎某人上台，或以掌声表示感谢
senses.example: Please applaud our next speaker as she comes to the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 下一位演讲者上台时，请大家鼓掌欢迎。
senses.why: The clap is directed at a person as a social gesture, extending the physical action to a ritual of welcome or thanks.
senses.whyCN: 掌声指向某个人，成为一种社交姿态；物理动作延伸为欢迎或致谢的仪式。

senses.title: To praise a performance or achievement publicly
senses.definition: to publicly praise a performance, work, or achievement, especially in the media
senses.definitionCN: 公开称赞演出、作品或成就，尤见于媒体报道
senses.example: Critics applauded the young director's first film.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家们盛赞这位年轻导演的首部电影。
senses.why: Approval that once needed clapping can now be expressed in words; the sound of praise replaces the sound of hands.
senses.whyCN: 原本需要鼓掌表达的赞许，如今可以用言语表达；赞许之声取代了拍手之声。

senses.title: To express strong approval of a decision or action
senses.definition: to say or show that you strongly approve of a decision, action, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 表示强烈赞成某个决定、行为或想法
senses.example: Environmental groups applauded the government's new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 环保团体对政府的新政策表示赞许。
senses.why: When the object is abstract, applaud no longer means clapping but standing behind something with approval.
senses.whyCN: 当宾语是抽象事物时，applaud 不再指拍手，而是表示对某事的认同与支持。

senses.title: To praise someone for a specific quality or effort
senses.titleCN: 因品质或努力而称赞某人
senses.definition: to praise a person for a particular quality, effort, or courage, often with for
senses.definitionCN: 常与 for 连用，因某种品质、努力或勇气而称赞某人
senses.example: Teachers applauded the students for their honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 老师们称赞学生诚实。
senses.why: The pattern applaud sb for sth treats praise as a reward given to a person, like applause given to a performer.
senses.whyCN: applaud sb for sth 结构把称赞看作给一个人的奖励，正如把掌声献给表演者。

senses.title: To be worthy of praise
senses.definition: to deserve praise, used in passive or descriptive sentences about actions or qualities
senses.definitionCN: 用于被动或描述性句子，指行为或品质值得称赞
senses.example: His courage in speaking up deserves to be applauded.
senses.exampleCN: 他敢于发声的勇气值得称道。
senses.why: Approval as a reward can be described as owed; something so good that it should receive the clap of praise.
senses.whyCN: 赞许作为一种奖励，可被描述为「应得的」；好到理应收获掌声的赞美。

intro.en: Applaud comes from Latin via Italian, built on a root meaning to clap or strike together.
intro.cn: applaud 经意大利语进入英语，词根义为「拍击；相击而响」。

items.en: Latin applaudere, from ad- (toward) + plaudere (to clap, strike), meaning to clap in approval.
items.cn: 拉丁语 applaudere，由 ad-（朝向）+ plaudere（拍击）构成，义为「拍手表示赞成」。

items.en: The compound verb spread in Late Latin and gave related forms like plausus, a clapping or a sound of approval.
items.cn: 这一复合动词在晚期拉丁语中通行，并派生出 plausus（拍打声；赞许声）等相关形式。

items.en: The word passed into Italian as applaudire before entering English.
items.cn: 该词先进入意大利语，作 applaudire，随后进入英语。

items.en: Applaud is first recorded in English in the late 1500s, at first meaning to clap or express approval.
items.cn: applaud 于十六世纪末在英语中首次见于记载，最初义为拍手或表示赞许。

items.en: The sense broadened from literal clapping to public and figurative praise of ideas, decisions, and people.
items.cn: 词义从字面鼓掌扩展为对想法、决定和人物的公开或比喻性称赞。

note.en: These words share spelling or meaning patterns with applaud, but differ in force or usage.
note.cn: 以下词语与 applaud 在拼写或词义上相关，但在语气或用法上有区别。

entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指鼓掌的声音；掌声

entries.definition: a round fruit; only looks similar at the start of the word
entries.definitionCN: 一种水果；仅词首拼写相近，与 applaud 词源无关

entries.definition: to make a formal request; shares the prefix ap- but has a different root
entries.definitionCN: 申请；应用；与前缀 ap- 相同但词根不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: seeming reasonable; from the same Latin root plaudere
entries.definitionCN: 看似有理的；与 applaud 同源于拉丁语 plaudere，原义与掌声相关

entries.definition: to hit the hands together; plainer and more physical than applaud
entries.definitionCN: 拍手；比 applaud 更口语、更侧重动作本身

entries.definition: to express strong approval in words; general-purpose praise
entries.definitionCN: 称赞；用言语表达赞许，泛用性最强

entries.definition: to shout in support or joy; louder and more emotional than clapping
entries.definitionCN: 欢呼；以喊叫表示支持或高兴，比鼓掌情绪更外放
嘉奖；正式或官方的称赞，语气庄重

normalIntro.en: Build the word from its Latin parts and sound family.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁语部件和声音家族来搭建这个词。

normal.en: ap- + plaud: the prefix ap- (toward) plus the root plaud (clap) makes 'clap toward someone'.
normal.cn: ap-（朝向）+ plaud（拍击）＝「朝某人拍手」，即鼓掌赞许。

normal.en: applause is the noun twin: you applaud, and the result is applause.
normal.cn: applause 是名词孪生兄弟：你 applaud（鼓掌），产生的就是 applause（掌声）。

normal.en: plausible shares the root plaud: what gets applause sounds plausible.
normal.cn: plausible 与 applaud 同根：能赢得掌声的说法，听起来就显得可信。

normal.en: Sound link: 'a-PLOD' — picture the audience plodding hands together again and again.
normal.cn: 读音联想「厄-普洛德」：想象观众双手像踏步一样一下一下拍个不停。

normal.en: Opposite pair: applaud to approve, boo to reject — a theatre needs both.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：applaud 表示赞成，boo 表示喝倒彩——剧院里两者都有。

abstract.en: Picture two hands meeting like friends shaking hands: approval made audible.
abstract.cn: 想象双手相会如友人握手：赞许被变成了声音。

abstract.en: Applaud is approval you can hear; praise is approval you can read.
abstract.cn: applaud 是听得见的赞许，praise 是读得到的赞许。

abstract.en: Think of a switch that turns liking into sound: press it, and the room claps.
abstract.cn: 把它想成把「喜欢」转换成声音的开关：一按，满堂掌声。

examples.en: The whole audience applauded when the singer came on stage.
examples.cn: 歌手登台时，全场观众鼓掌。

examples.en: We applaud her decision to continue her studies.
examples.cn: 我们赞许她继续深造的决定。

examples.en: His speech was warmly applauded by the teachers.
examples.cn: 他的演讲赢得老师们热烈的掌声。

sensesIntro.en: From the physical clap, the word grows into welcoming, praising, and approving.

branches.en: Praise in words replaces clapping for works and performances.

branches.en: Approval extends to decisions, policies, and ideas.

branches.en: Praise becomes personal: applauding someone for a quality.
branches.cn: 称赞变得具体：因某种品质而称赞某人。

branches.en: Approval turns into a reward that good actions deserve.

intro.en: Applaud is built from a Latin prefix and a sound-related root, with a small word family.

latinIntro.en: The Latin root plaud- also appears in other English and Latin words about striking and approval.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 plaud- 还出现在其他与拍击、赞许相关的英语及拉丁语词中。

senses.title: A device for a specific job

senses.title: A person who applies for a job

senses.title: A person making a formal request

definition_zh: 申请；申请书；应用；涂抹；专注

scene: 他把简历和表格装进信封，写上面试单位的地址。Her application arrived before the deadline.

senses.title: A formal request
senses.definition: a written or spoken request for a job, a place, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 为职位、名额或服务提出的书面或口头请求
senses.example: Her application arrived before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 她的申请在截止日期前寄到了。
senses.why: Application is the noun of apply, and the oldest formal sense is the act of asking, which then named the papers carrying the request.
senses.whyCN: application 是 apply 的名词，最早的正式义就是「提出请求」这一行为，之后又指承载请求的文件。

senses.title: The act of putting to use
senses.definition: the use of an idea, method, or substance in a practical situation
senses.definitionCN: 把观念、方法或物质用于实际情形
senses.example: The application of this theory is not simple.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论的应用并不简单。
senses.why: To apply is literally to lay something onto a surface, so application keeps the image of a method being laid onto a problem.
senses.whyCN: apply 字面就是把某物贴到一个表面上，所以 application 保留了「把方法贴到问题上」的意象。

senses.title: A substance spread on
senses.definition: a quantity of cream, paint, or medicine put onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 涂在表面上的一定量的乳霜、颜料或药物
senses.example: A thin application of oil will protect the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 薄薄涂一层油可以保护木材。
senses.why: The physical sense of laying something on survives in this concrete use of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 把东西贴上去的物理含义，在这个具体的名词用法中保留下来。

senses.title: Close attention to a task
senses.definition: the quality of giving steady attention to work or study
senses.definitionCN: 对工作或学习持续投入注意力的品质
senses.example: Success here depends on steady application.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的成功取决于持续的专注。
senses.why: If the mind is applied to a task, it is bent onto it, and that effort became a sense of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 如果心思被「贴」在任务上，就是弯着身子扑在上面，这种用力成了名词的一个义项。

definition_zh: 申请；应用；涂抹；适用
definition_en: to make a formal request, to put something to use, to spread something on, or to be relevant
core_image: 把一层颜料均匀刷到木板上
scene: 刷墙的师傅把滚筒按进漆里，再一点点推上去。Apply the paint in thin layers.
sceneCN: 这里 apply 是「涂抹」（第 3 个义项：把某物敷到表面）；句意是把颜料薄薄地涂上几层。

senses.title: To make a formal request
senses.definition: to ask officially for a job, a place, or permission
senses.definitionCN: 正式请求职位、名额或许可
senses.example: She applied for a place at the college.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了这所学院的一个名额。
senses.why: Latin applicare meant 'to attach oneself to', and a candidate who applies attaches himself to an institution by request.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 applicare 意为「使自己附着于」，提出申请的候选人正是用请求把自己附着到某个机构上。

senses.title: To put something to use
senses.definition: to use a rule, method, or idea in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情形中使用规则、方法或观念
senses.example: He applied the same method to a harder problem.
senses.exampleCN: 他把同样的方法用到更难的题上。
senses.why: The original image is laying one thing onto another, so applying a method is laying it onto a case.
senses.whyCN: 本来的意象是把一样东西贴到另一样上，所以 apply 一个方法就是把它贴到一个情形上。

senses.title: To spread something on a surface
senses.definition: to put a substance such as paint or cream onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把颜料、乳霜等物质涂到表面上
senses.example: Apply the paint in thin layers.
senses.exampleCN: 把颜料薄薄地涂上几层。
senses.why: This is the most physical sense and the closest to the Latin verb's literal meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这是最物理的义项，也最接近拉丁语动词的字面含义。

senses.title: To be relevant to
senses.definition: to concern or be valid for a person or case
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某情形有关，或对其有效
senses.example: The ban applies to all vehicles.
senses.exampleCN: 这项禁令适用于所有车辆。
senses.why: If a rule can be laid onto a case, the rule reaches that case, which is the intransitive sense with to.
senses.whyCN: 如果一条规则能贴到一个情形上，这条规则就触及该情形，这就是与 to 连用的不及物用法。

senses.title: To choose someone for a post

senses.example: The board appointed her as director.

sensesIntro.en: Fixing something at a point gives both the agreed time and the assigned post.
sensesIntro.cn: 把事物定在某个点上，既产生约定时间，也产生任命职位。

intro.en: A French-derived verb built on the Latin word for a point.

latinIntro.en: The root punctum, 'point', also gives punctual and puncture.

definition_zh: 约会；预约；任命；职位
definition_en: an arranged meeting, or the act of giving someone a job or position
core_image: 日程本上写着时间和地点的那个格子
scene: 她翻开工位旁的日程本，看了看下午那一栏。I have an appointment with the dentist at four.

pos.zh: 名词：约会；预约；任命；职位

senses.title: An arranged meeting
senses.definition: a fixed time and place to meet someone
senses.definitionCN: 与人见面的约定时间和地点
senses.example: I have an appointment with the dentist at four.
senses.exampleCN: 我四点约了牙医。
senses.why: Appointment is appoint plus -ment, and the older sense of appoint was 'to settle a time', so the noun first named the settling and then the meeting fixed.
senses.whyCN: appointment 是 appoint 加 -ment，而 appoint 的较早义是「议定时间」，所以名词先指这个议定，再指定下来的会面。

senses.title: The act of naming to office
senses.definition: the act of officially choosing someone for a position
senses.definitionCN: 正式选定某人担任某职的行为
senses.example: Her appointment as head of school surprised nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 她被任命为校长，没有人感到意外。
senses.why: The same noun also records the official act, because appointing is itself a kind of settling.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也记录这个正式行为，因为任命本身就是一种「定下来」。

senses.title: A post or office
senses.definition: the job to which a person has been appointed
senses.definitionCN: 被任命担任的工作或职务
senses.example: He accepted a teaching appointment in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 他接受了北方的一份教职。
senses.why: By transference the settled position itself came to be called an appointment.
senses.whyCN: 通过转喻，被定下来的那个位置本身也被称作 appointment。

core.cn: 核心意象：日历上被标记的一个点。

definition_zh: v. 分派；分摊；按比例分配（责任、费用、名额等）
definition_en: To divide something into shares and give each party its part according to a rule or standard, used especially of costs, blame, seats and resources.
core_image: 把一整块按份切开，谁该拿多少就分多少
scene: 委员会按各校人数分摊这笔经费。The committee will apportion the grant according to enrolment.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：apportion 指按某个标准把总量分给各方，宾语常是费用、责任或名额。

senses.title: Share out by a rule
senses.definition: to divide a total into parts and give each person or group the share that a standard says is theirs
senses.definitionCN: 把总量切成若干份，按某个标准把各方应得的那一份分给他们
senses.example: The treaty apportioned the fishing rights between the two states.
senses.exampleCN: 条约在两国之间分配了捕鱼权。
senses.why: The word is ap- plus portion, literally to hand out portions, so a rule for dividing is always implied.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 ap- 加 portion，字面就是「把一份份递出去」，因此总隐含着一条划分标准。

senses.title: Assign blame or duty
senses.definition: to decide how much of the fault or responsibility belongs to each party involved
senses.definitionCN: 判定参与的各方各应承担多少过错或责任
senses.example: The inquiry refused to apportion blame before the evidence was complete.
senses.exampleCN: 在证据齐备之前，调查委员会拒绝归派过错。
senses.why: Here nothing physical is cut: the same picture of dividing a whole is applied to fault, which is why the verb sounds formal and legal.
senses.whyCN: 这里切的不是实物：同一幅「分整块」的画面被用在过错上，所以这个动词听起来正式、带法律味。

intro.en: Apportion is ap-, to, plus portion, from Latin portio, a share, which is related to pars, a part. English took it from Old French apportioner.
intro.cn: apportion 是 ap-「向」加 portion，后者来自拉丁语 portio「一份」，与 pars「部分」同源。英语从古法语 apportioner 借入。

items.en: Latin pars meant a part or a share of a whole. It gives part, partial, particle, apart and parcel.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pars 意为整体的「一部分、一份」。它产生 part、partial、particle、apart 与 parcel。

items.en: Portio named a measured share, the portion handed to one person out of a common stock.
items.cn: portio 指量好的一份，即从公共总量中递给某个人的那一份。

items.en: Old French portion kept the sense of a share, especially of food served to one diner.
items.cn: 古法语 portion 保留「一份」之义，尤指端给一位用餐者的那份食物。

items.en: Adding a-, to, gave apportioner, to deal out shares, the verb English later borrowed.
items.cn: 加上 a-「向」得到 apportioner「把份额分出去」，这就是英语后来借入的动词。

items.en: English recorded apportion in the 1570s, used from the start for dividing costs, land and duties.
items.cn: 英语在 1570 年代记录到 apportion，一开始就用于分摊费用、划分土地与职责。

items.en: Today apportion is common in law and public finance, with apportionment naming the act of dividing seats or funds.
items.cn: 如今 apportion 常见于法律与公共财政，名词 apportionment 指分配席位或资金这一行为。

note.en: The look-alike group separates apportion from appoint, which means to name someone to a post; the near-meaning group lists other verbs of sharing out.
note.cn: 形近组把 apportion 与 appoint「任命」区分开；近义组列出其他表示「分出去」的动词。

normalIntro.en: Apportion is ap- plus portion: hand a portion to each person, so the whole gets shared out by a rule.
normalIntro.cn: apportion 就是 ap- 加 portion：给每人递上一份，整块就按规则分完了。

normal.en: The usual objects are blame, costs, seats and resources.

normal.en: It is formal: in speech say share out or split.

normal.en: Do not confuse apportion with appoint, to give a job.

normal.en: The pattern is apportion something among or between parties.

abstract.en: Imagine a bill split by how much each person ate.

abstract.en: Think of seats handed out by population.

examples.cn: 费用按建筑面积分摊。

examples.en: The board is apportioning next year's budget.
examples.cn: 董事会正在分配明年的预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ap-「向」+ portion「一份」——朝每位递上一份，按比例分完，就是分摊 apportion。

root: 拉丁语 pars「部分」生出 portio「一份」，古法语作 portion；加前缀 a-「向」成 apportioner「把份额分出去」，英语作 apportion，字面即「分成一份份给出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one act of dividing: cutting a real total into shares, and cutting fault or duty into shares the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种划分动作：把实际总量切成份额，以及用同样方式把过错或职责切成份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one whole cut into shares, each party getting what the rule says
